plan.contextChunk: This figure places two oblique triangles side by side in plain black outline, lettered identically, to contrast where the altitude lands. In each one the horizontal base is labeled b and runs from the vertex alpha at the left to the vertex gamma at the right, the apex is labeled beta, the short left side from alpha to beta is labeled c, and the long side sloping from beta down to gamma is labeled a. In the left triangle the apex sits above the interior of the base, and a dashed vertical altitude labeled h drops from beta to a point on b, meeting it at a small square marking the right angle; an arc at alpha marks the interior angle. In the right triangle the apex has shifted left beyond alpha, making the angle there obtuse, so the dashed altitude falls outside the figure and the base is carried leftward by a dashed extension to receive its foot. Two arcs appear at that lower left corner, one for the interior angle alpha and, immediately left of it, one for the angle alpha prime between side c and the extension. Setting the arrangements against each other shows that the same height construction serves both, provided the angle used is the one adjacent to the perpendicular, which supplies h for computing the area of a triangle with no right angle of its own.

interactionPlan.concept: In any oblique triangle the altitude h from the apex gives the height used in area and sine-rule formulas, but when the angle at α is obtuse that altitude falls outside the triangle onto an extension of the base, where the supplementary angle α′ is the one adjacent to the perpendicular.
elements: Left panel: acute-case triangle drawn in solid black outline with vertices α (lower left), γ (lower right), β (apex above the interior of the base)
Horizontal base segment from α to γ labeled b, centered below the segment
Left side from α up to β labeled c, placed outside the side near its midpoint
Right side sloping from β down to γ labeled a, placed above/outside the side
Dashed vertical altitude from β to a foot point on segment b, labeled h to the right of the dashed line
Small square right-angle marker at the foot of the altitude, opening toward α
Single arc at vertex α marking the interior angle, with the Greek label α just outside
Vertex labels β (above apex), α (left of lower-left vertex), γ (right of lower-right vertex) in italic serif
Right panel: obtuse-case triangle with the same lettering, apex β shifted left so it lies beyond α and the interior angle at α is obtuse
Dashed horizontal extension of the base running leftward from α to the foot of the altitude
Dashed vertical altitude from β down to that exterior foot, labeled h on its left
Small square right-angle marker where the exterior altitude meets the dashed extension
Two arcs at the lower-left corner: the larger interior angle α between side c and base b, and immediately left of it the angle α′ between side c and the dashed base extension
Labels α and α′ set beside their respective arcs
White background, no axes, no legend, all strokes thin black, auxiliary construction lines dashed

interactions.label: Horizontal position of apex β
interactions.teaches: That the altitude foot slides continuously along the base line as β moves, crossing α at the exact moment the angle at α becomes right and then obtuse, so the altitude is the same construction in every case — only its landing point changes.

interactions.label: Case
interactions.teaches: That the dashed base extension and the angle α′ are needed only in the obtuse case, and that α′ is the angle actually adjacent to the perpendicular there.
That clicking the base b drops the perpendicular from β and reveals the right-angle marker, turning the oblique triangle into a right triangle whose leg h is the height used in area = ½·b·h.

demo_steps.title: An oblique triangle
demo_steps.narration: A triangle with base b from α to γ and apex β — no right angle anywhere. To find its area we still need a height.

demo_steps.title: Drop the altitude
demo_steps.narration: Click on base b: a dashed perpendicular h falls from β and a small square marks the right angle. The oblique triangle now contains a right triangle with legs h and part of b.

demo_steps.title: Slide β toward α
demo_steps.narration: Drag the apex left. The foot of the altitude travels along the base toward α while h stays perpendicular to the base line.

demo_steps.title: Past α: the foot leaves the triangle
demo_steps.narration: When β passes to the left of α, the angle at α becomes obtuse and the altitude foot lands off the base — the base line must be extended by a dashed segment to catch it.

demo_steps.title: The angle α′ adjacent to the perpendicular
demo_steps.narration: In the obtuse case two arcs appear: the interior angle α and its supplement α′ between c and the extension. It is α′ that sits in the right triangle, and sin α′ = sin α, so h = c·sin α either way.

demo_steps.title: Compare both cases
demo_steps.narration: Seen side by side, the two constructions are the same move: drop a perpendicular from β to the line containing b. Only whether the foot lands inside or outside the triangle differs.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The height of a triangle is measured to the line containing the base, not to the base segment itself — so h = c·sin α works for obtuse triangles too, because the exterior angle α′ that actually forms the right triangle has exactly the same sine as α.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two clean line-art triangles on white, side by side, both wider than tall with the base horizontal. Left triangle: apex β roughly one-third of the way along the base and well above it; sides c (short, left) and a (long, right) labeled outside their midpoints; base labeled b below center; a vertical dashed altitude h from β with a small open square right-angle marker at its foot on b; a single small arc at α. Right triangle: identical lettering but the apex β sits left of and above α, so the left side c leans back to the right and the interior angle at α is clearly obtuse; the base is continued leftward with a dashed horizontal segment reaching under β, and the dashed altitude h drops from β onto that extension with a right-angle square at the foot; two adjacent arcs at the lower-left corner label α (interior, larger, opening right) and α′ (between c and the dashed extension, opening left). All geometry in thin black stroke; construction lines (altitude, base extension) dashed; vertex and side labels in italic serif, Greek letters for vertices, lowercase a, b, c, h for sides and height. When an interactive case is active, highlight the current right triangle (h, base-segment, and c) with a light accent fill so the learner sees the embedded right triangle emerge; keep everything else black-on-white.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for moving vertex beta: the learner drags the apex horizontally across alpha, the altitude foot moves from inside the base to outside on the dashed extension, showing why the height construction changes position for acute versus obtuse arrangements.
- Toggle between acute and obtuse angle views: the learner switches the named case, the base extension and alpha prime label appear only in the obtuse view, making clear which adjacent angle supplies the perpendicular height.

authoredContext:
Now that we can solve a triangle for missing values, we can use some of those values and the sine function to find the area of an oblique triangle. Recall that the area formula for a triangle is given as Area= 1 2 bh, where b is base and h is height. For oblique triangles, we must find h before we can use the area formula. Observing the two triangles in the figure, one acute and one obtuse, we can drop a perpendicular to represent the height and then apply the trigonometric property sinα= opposite hypotenuse to write an equation for area in oblique triangles. In the acute triangle, we have sinα= h c or csinα=h. However, in the obtuse triangle, we drop the perpendicular outside the triangle and extend the base b to form a right triangle. The angle used in calculation is α ′, or 180−α.

Two oblique triangles with standard labels. Both have a dotted altitude line h extended from angle beta to the horizontal base side b. In the first, which is an acute triangle, the altitude is within the triangle. In the second, which is an obtuse triangle, the altitude h is outside of the triangle.

The construction

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Rendered at ~half the available width with a 960×300 viewBox, so both triangles and all their italic labels (α, β, γ, a, b, c, h, α′) appear very small — noticeably less legible than the source, whose lettering is prominent.

In the obtuse (right) panel the generated figure draws a small right-angle square at the foot of the altitude; the source right panel shows only the dashed extension and dashed h with no right-angle marker.

In side-by-side mode the right panel's apex offset is derived from the left panel's slider value (t = −max(0.05, m·0.25)), giving a very short dashed base extension — shorter and less visually explicit than the source, where the extension and the α′ arc are clearly separated.
The generated obtuse panel places 'h' quite close to the dashed altitude and the 'c' label, slightly crowding the α′ arc region compared with the cleaner spacing in the source.
Optional blue shading of the embedded right triangle and the numeric readout panel are additions not present in the source (off by default, so low impact).
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful two-panel reproduction (acute vs. obtuse altitude construction) with correct lettering and a rich, genuinely pedagogical set of interactions (slider, case selector, altitude/shade toggles, 7-step player, clickable sides with popups); the main weakness is that the drawing occupies only part of the canvas so labels render uncomfortably small, plus a spurious right-angle square in the obtuse panel.
action_items: Tighten the viewBox (or enlarge the panels within it) so the triangles fill the available width and label font size reads at ≥12px effective on screen.
Remove the right-angle square from the obtuse panel default view (or make it appear only when the 'altitude' explanation step highlights the perpendicular), matching the source.
Give the right panel an independent, larger negative apex offset in side-by-side mode so the dashed base extension and α′ arc are as clearly visible as in the source.
Nudge the 'h' and 'c' labels apart in the obtuse panel and keep the α/α′ arc labels clear of the dashed extension.

feedback.rationale: Concept and interaction structure are sound (concept 5, no failure modes); remaining issues are implementation details like viewBox sizing, label spacing, and a spurious right-angle marker.

attempts.html:
The construction

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Composition: the source places the two triangles side by side in a wide strip; the default render stacks them vertically (the side-by-side branch only triggers when W/H ≥ 1.7, and the wide control panel squeezes the canvas), so the at-a-glance layout differs from the source.

In the obtuse panel the interior arc at α is drawn noticeably larger/wider than in the source (where α and α′ arcs are small and nearly equal radius), and the α label floats higher above the arc than the source's tight in-place labelling.
The right-angle square in the acute panel is drawn quite small and tight against the base compared with the source's clearly visible square marker at the foot of h.

Added elements not in the source: an optional blue shaded embedded right triangle, a numeric readout panel (α, sin α, h, area) and multi-step narration text — off/side-panel by default, but they add chrome beyond the original line drawing.

In the obtuse panel the dashed base extension in the source runs the full way from the foot to α at the same level as b with a clear gap; here it is shorter and the 'h' label sits very close to the left canvas edge.
evaluation.notes: Faithful, well-labelled reproduction of both the acute and obtuse altitude constructions with a rich, genuinely pedagogical set of interactions (apex slider, case selector, altitude/shading toggles, 7-step player, clickable side/arc popups); main weaknesses are the default vertical stacking instead of the source's side-by-side layout and some oversized/offset angle-arc and label styling in the obtuse panel.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; remaining issues are implementation details (default side-by-side layout threshold/canvas sizing, arc radii, label offsets, right-angle marker size) that belong to the generator.

discrepancies: In the obtuse (right) panel the apex β is offset much less to the left than in the source, so the dashed base extension is very short and the α / α′ arcs plus the c label are crowded into a small wedge; the source has a clearly visible dashed extension and well-separated arcs.
The generated obtuse panel draws a solid right-angle square at the external foot; the source marks the right angle only in the left (acute) panel, leaving the outside foot as a plain dashed corner.

Overall figure scale: with the docked control panel occupying nearly half the width, both triangles render considerably smaller than in the source, making the italic serif labels (a, b, c, h, α, β, γ) noticeably smaller than the source's prominent lettering.
The right panel's h dashed segment appears to start at β and run down almost coincident with side c near the apex, whereas in the source h and c visibly diverge from β with clear separation.
Extra narrative text block and numeric readout (sin α, h = c·sin α, area) accompany the figure; these are not in the source, though they sit outside the drawing area.
evaluation.notes: A faithful two-panel reconstruction of the acute/obtuse altitude figure with correct lettering, dashed altitude, base extension and α/α′ arcs, plus a rich and pedagogically apt set of interactions; main weaknesses are the under-shifted obtuse apex (crowded arcs and a too-short extension) and generally small label/figure scale.
action_items: Increase the obtuse offset (make tObtuse track the slider more directly, e.g. down to ~-0.3 of the base) so the dashed extension and the α / α′ arcs are as separated as in the source.
Suppress the right-angle square at the external foot (or draw it in dashed style) to match the source's right panel, which marks the square only in the acute case.

Enlarge the drawing viewport / font scale so the triangles fill more of the available area and the italic labels read comfortably at inline size; nudge the right panel's h label and c label apart from side c.
Ensure the h dashed line in the obtuse panel is visually distinct from side c near β (small stroke offset or lighter dash spacing) as in the source.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; the remaining issues (obtuse apex offset, extraneous right-angle marker, label/figure scale, overlapping h and c) are concrete rendering fixes.
